AccountEnv.description: Which Midas environment an account targets (D-N1 / SDK §3.2).
AccountEnv.title: AccountEnv

AccountStatus.description:
Account vault lifecycle — also the worker claim state machine (D-15):
CONNECTING is the claimable PENDING, RUNNING the in-flight claim, CONNECTED/
FAILED the finalise terminals, EXPIRED the relogin loop's unrefreshable marker.

REVOKED is the operator terminal — set only by an explicit back-office revoke,
never by the worker. The worker only ever claims CONNECTING, so a REVOKED row
is never claimed; account-selection (``first_connected``) filters CONNECTED,
so a REVOKED row is never handed to redeem / buy-links either.
AccountStatus.title: AccountStatus

ActivateByDenominationRequest.description:
Activate using a stocked code of a denomination — no explicit code on input.

The service picks a RANDOM available code of ``(game, denomination_value)``
from the caller's inventory and drives a standalone activation with it; the
customer never names a specific code (D-33).
ActivateByDenominationRequest.title: ActivateByDenominationRequest

BatchActivateByDenominationRequest.description:
Activate up to ``quantity`` random stocked codes of a denomination in one call.

Each unit is one activation and consumes one activation from the account-master
quota. ``quantity`` is hard-capped at 1000 here and further bounded by the
server's ``batch_max_size`` setting. When the quota is short, the global
``batch_strict_quota_check`` flag decides between a trimmed batch and an
overspend (see the service).
BatchActivateByDenominationRequest.title: BatchActivateByDenominationRequest

BatchActivationAccepted.description:
Batch outcome — how many were requested vs actually accepted, and their ids.

``accepted`` can be below ``requested`` when the batch was trimmed to the
remaining quota (strict) or ran out of stocked codes.
BatchActivationAccepted.title: BatchActivationAccepted

BatchStatusResult.description:
The rows that resolved, plus the ids that did not.

Unknown and cross-customer ids both land in ``missing`` — indistinguishable,
so the endpoint cannot be used as an id oracle.
BatchStatusResult.title: BatchStatusResult

Character.description: The in-game role resolved for a looked-up player id.
Character.title: Character

CharacterList.description: Pageable list of characters for an account + game.
CharacterList.title: CharacterList

CodeStatus.description:
A stocked redeem code's lifecycle.

AVAILABLE → RESERVED (atomic reserve into a task) → USED (activation SUCCESS)
or back to AVAILABLE (activation non-SUCCESS, released by the aggregator).
INVALID marks a code rejected by shape validation on import.
CodeStatus.title: CodeStatus

Country.description: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 subset the gateway accepts as a region.
Country.title: Country

TaskState.description:
Aggregate task lifecycle. PENDING/RUNNING are non-terminal; the three
terminals are decided by the aggregator from the per-item outcomes (D-38):
SUCCESS (all ok), PARTIAL (mixed), FAILED (none).
TaskState.title: TaskState

info.description: Public API for Midasbuy code activation and in-game currency purchases.
info.title: Midasbuy API

post.description:
Async connect: the account is owned by the caller's customer
(``customer.id``); ``sub.id`` is retained as the originating billing key.

Funnels through the shared idempotency lock (D-12): a retried connect with the
same ``Idempotency-Key`` replays the stored ``202`` instead of spawning a
duplicate account row + CONNECT job in Midas.

get.description: Fetch one of the caller's accounts; a cross-scope miss is a neutral 404.
List the caller's accounts, newest first, paginated, obfuscated.
List the games the catalog supports; read-only, bearer-authed.
Fetch one item by its opaque ``item_id``; a miss is a neutral ``404``.
List the purchasable catalog items for one ``game``, paginated.

Return cached characters for ``account_id`` + ``game``.

Always empty in SDK v2 (no list-characters method). Use ``/lookup`` with a
known ``player_id`` or supply ``player_id`` on ``/redeem/activate`` directly.
Resolve the in-game role for ``player_id`` in ``game`` (scoped to the caller).
get.summary: Look up a character by player id

post.description:
Enqueue a character-list refresh for the account.

SDK v2 dropped bulk character listing — this endpoint validates the account
is connected and returns 202; the list will remain empty until the SDK
exposes a list method again. Customers should pass ``player_id`` directly
on ``/redeem/activate`` for UC codes.

Stock one or many codes (caps + dedup + encryption); idempotent.

Stock is owned by the account (``customer_id``); the bearer key only
namespaces the idempotency lock (unchanged). Request/response shapes are
unchanged — the internal scope is the customer.

get.description: List the account's stock, newest first, paginated + filterable, obfuscated.
Aggregate available/total stock per game + denomination, paginated (account pool).
get.summary: Summarize stock per game and denomination

post.description:
Async single redeem: persist + enqueue, return ``202`` with the id.

The bearer key is the billing key + idempotency namespace (unchanged); the
owning customer is resolved from it and owns the activation.

Async batch redeem of up to ``quantity`` random stocked codes.

One activation is enqueued per granted unit; ``accepted`` reports how many
the quota + stock actually allowed (trimmed when ``batch_strict_quota_check``
is on, or fewer if stock ran out). One ``Idempotency-Key`` covers the batch.
post.summary: Activate up to N codes by denomination in one batch

post.description:
Async redeem of a RANDOM stocked code of a denomination.

Identical envelope to ``/activate`` but the body names ``denomination_value``
instead of a code: the service atomically reserves a random AVAILABLE code of
``(game, denomination_value)`` from the account pool, then persists +
enqueues. A ``409 code_out_of_stock`` means no such code is in stock.

get.description: Fetch one of the account's activations; a cross-account miss is a neutral 404.
List the account's activations across its keys, newest first, paginated.

post.description:
Statuses for up to 100 ids in one call — the alternative to polling ``/get``.

A POST despite being a read: the id list is a body, not a query string. It
carries no ``Idempotency-Key`` (nothing is mutated) but IS rate-limited far
harder than a single read — the burn happens before the query, so an
over-budget caller never touches the database. Ids that are unknown or owned
by someone else come back in ``missing`` rather than as an error.

get.description:
Return the caller's own subscription status.

Reports the plan type, the effective status (active/expired/suspended),
the expiry timestamp, the remaining quota and the per-minute rate limit.

post.description: Batch activate N codes across players → one task + N activations (202).

get.description: Aggregate + per-item status for one of the caller's tasks; a miss is 404.
List the caller's tasks (aggregate only), newest first, paginated.

post.description: Compose the exact code set for a target amount → one task + N activations (202).
